## Overview

Move Qwen3.5 models and MTP on XPU to the eager, breakable-graph design introduced by [vLLM #51012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51012). Recover small-batch MoE decode fusion by calling the routed/shared expert provider from [vllm-xpu-kernels #670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/670) directly in the XPU model, without model-level `torch.compile` or a compiler fusion pass. Fusion is bounded to eligible 1–8-token FP16/BF16 calls with per-tensor FP8-e4m3 weights; the routed/shared expert outputs share one TP reduction. Other configurations retain the existing MoE path.

## Claims

- TP2, async, graph-on MoE B1: streamed TPOT **-21.0% to -20.1%**, output throughput **+16.3% to +25.4%** for 1K/8K/32K input and 512 output tokens versus the compiled XPU baseline.

## Validation

Environment: two Intel Xe2 GPUs, 32 GB per card, cards 0/1, TP2, PyTorch `2.14.0+xpu`, FP16 with online `fp8_per_tensor` quantization. Performance checkpoints: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE)**, using the Qwen3.5 implementation, and **Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B**, measured at **BF16, no quantization, TP1 on card 0**, with TP2 greedy checks on cards 0/1.

Baseline: main `fa3b9d1377`, original XPU model with `VLLM_COMPILE` (mode 3). This PR: `dd6f1ccb15`, XPU eager model (mode 0). Both use the same kernel build (`0becdcc76c`, the #670 Qwen native implementations). Matching serving flags: async scheduling, prefix caching off, block size 64, max model length 40960, max batched tokens 8192 and max sequences 128. Offline runs use max sequences 32. Graph-on is `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

### End-to-end serving (`vllm bench serve`)

Random workload follows #51012: 320/384/512 prompts at concurrency 32/64/128, 128-token input and 256-token output; 128 prompts at cc32 for the 4K-context case; 16 prompts for single-stream decode and 4K/8 prefill. Real MoE prompts use a fixed, balanced 32-row subset of SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k`, 512 output tokens; this is a subset measurement.

### Isolated forward and MTP

Same `LLM.generate` workloads as `vllm bench latency`: two warmups and five measured iterations. Decode step = `(t[32/65] - t[32/1]) / 64`; prefill = `t[4096/1]`. Decode/MTP values are ordered **B1 / B32**; prefill values are ordered **B1 / B8**, matching #51012. MTP uses one speculative token.

Regressions above 1% in this measurement: qwen35_9b nv_decode_cc128. The headline improvement is specific to the stated MoE B1 workload.

### Correctness

- Native fused/fallback/TP2 model-block tests: **18 passed**. Existing model/platform/quantization tests: **6 passed**.
- Real-weight TP2 reload/graph regression: **1 passed**, retaining plan, workspace and captured addresses after reload (`rtol=atol=1e-2`). Missing-provider stock-wheel fallback: **1 passed**. Changed-file ruff, mypy, SPDX and test-tethering hooks passed. The native Buildkite source-build job still requires CI validation.
- Completed MTP jobs verify nonzero drafted and accepted tokens through the engine's metrics.

Greedy smoke: four identical prompts, temperature 0, up to 64 tokens, EOS respected. Counts below compare raw token IDs, including EOS.

|---|---|---:|

Some greedy outputs differ; token-exact equivalence is not established. The 64-token limit also truncates some smoke outputs.

Additional accuracy benchmarks are drawn from [RFC #59665](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59665). Full MoE evaluations use thinking enabled, greedy sampling, seed 0 and concurrency at most 8 to exercise small-token fusion. GSM8K: 5-shot, 16K output budget; GPQA-Diamond: 32K budget, high reasoning requested; AIME25: 32K budget, pass@1 avg1. AIME accepts boxed answers or the last integer in the completed final answer. Truncated answers are graded incorrect. Both sides use the same examples and prompts.

|---|---:|---:|---:|

| 35B-A3B / AIME25 avg1 | 17/30 (56.67%) | 16/30 (53.33%) | -3.33 |

9B correctness follows #51012's TP1/TP2 greedy checks; full 9B reasoning evaluations are not claimed.

### Reproduce

Use the same checkpoint and #670-capable kernel installation in both source trees. Run each server separately; set `PYTHON_BIN` when reusing a virtualenv.

```bash
# This PR, run from its source checkout:
MODEL_PATH=/path/to/checkpoint MODEL_NAME=benchmark-model bash server.sh
# Compiled baseline, run from the baseline checkout:
BREAKABLE=0 COMPILE_MODE=3 MODEL_PATH=/path/to/checkpoint MODEL_NAME=benchmark-model bash server.sh
# Second terminal: additional MoE small-batch sweep.
INPUT_LENGTHS=1024,8192,32768 BATCHES=1,2,4,8 bash client.sh benchmark-model 8000 results
# Graph-off: add GRAPH_MODE=NONE MAX_SEQS=8 MAX_BATCHED_TOKENS=1024 to either server.
# 9B server: add TP=1 DTYPE=bfloat16 QUANTIZATION=none ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0.
# NVIDIA-style serving cases, per source tree and model:
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model /path/to/checkpoint --served-model-name benchmark-model \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --dataset-name random --ignore-eos --seed 0 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 320 --max-concurrency 32 \
  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 256 --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
# Also 384@cc64, 512@cc128; 128@cc32 with input 4096; 16@cc1 with 128/256 or 4096/8.
# Equivalent isolated-forward workloads (same source tree, dtype/TP/quantization flags):
VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 vllm bench latency --model /path/to/checkpoint \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype float16 --quantization fp8_per_tensor \
  --language-model-only --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN --seed 0 --input-len 32 --output-len 65 \
  --batch-size 1 --num-iters-warmup 2 --num-iters 5 --max-model-len 40960 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --block-size 64 --no-enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
# Decode: output lengths 1/65 at B1/32. Prefill: input/output 4096/1 at B1/8.
# MTP: add --speculative-config '{"method":"qwen3_5_mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'.
# 9B latency: use TP1, BF16, and omit --quantization.
# Baseline latency: VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0 and compilation mode 3.
ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu FI_PROVIDER=tcp FI_TCP_IFACE=lo \
  CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=pidfd .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py \
  -k 'xpu_qwen3_5 and not missing_provider' -q
# Real-weight reload/graph regression:
VLLM_TEST_QWEN35_MODEL=/path/to/checkpoint VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
  ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu FI_PROVIDER=tcp FI_TCP_IFACE=lo \
  CCL_ZE_IPC_EXCHANGE=pidfd .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_qwen3_5.py -k reload_graph -q
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source_dir=${VLLM_SOURCE_DIR:-$PWD}
exec "${PYTHON_BIN:-$source_dir/.venv/bin/python}" - "${1:?model name}" "${2:-8000}" "${3:-results}" <<'PYCLIENT'
import json, os, random, statistics, sys, threading, time, urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
model, port, destination = sys.argv[1:]
out = Path(destination)
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
def request(prompt, barrier):
    payload = dict(model=model, prompt=prompt, max_tokens=512, temperature=0,
                   seed=0, ignore_eos=True, stream=True, return_token_ids=True,
                   stream_options={"include_usage": True})
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1/completions",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    client = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))
    first = last = usage = None
    tokens = 0
    barrier.wait(timeout=30)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    with client.open(req, timeout=900) as response:
        for line in response:
            if not line.startswith(b"data: "):
                continue
            data = line[6:].strip()
            if data == b"[DONE]":
                break
            chunk = json.loads(data)
            if chunk.get("error"):
                raise RuntimeError(chunk["error"])
            usage = chunk.get("usage") or usage
            for choice in chunk.get("choices", []):
                ids = choice.get("token_ids") or []
                if ids:
                    last = time.perf_counter()
                    first = last if first is None else first
                    tokens += len(ids)
    end = time.perf_counter()
    assert usage and usage["prompt_tokens"] == len(prompt)
    assert usage["completion_tokens"] == tokens == 512 and last > first
    return dict(start=start, end=end, tpot_ms=(last-first)*1000/511,
                ttft_ms=(first-start)*1000, output_tokens=tokens)
summaries = []
for length in map(int, os.environ.get("INPUT_LENGTHS", "1024,8192,32768").split(",")):
    rng = random.Random(0)
    prompt = [rng.randrange(1000, 20000) for _ in range(length)]
    for batch in map(int, os.environ.get("BATCHES", "1,2,4,8").split(",")):
        rounds = []
        for index in range(4):  # One warmup, three measured rounds.
            barrier = threading.Barrier(batch)
            with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=batch) as pool:
                requests = list(pool.map(lambda _: request(prompt, barrier), range(batch)))
            assert max(r["start"] for r in requests) < min(r["end"] for r in requests)
            elapsed = max(r["end"] for r in requests)-min(r["start"] for r in requests)
            rounds.append(dict(round=index, requests=requests,
                tpot_ms=statistics.mean(r["tpot_ms"] for r in requests),
                ttft_ms=statistics.mean(r["ttft_ms"] for r in requests),
                output_tok_s=batch*512/elapsed))
        summary = dict(input_tokens=length, batch=batch, rounds=rounds,
            median={k: statistics.median(r[k] for r in rounds[1:])
                    for k in ["tpot_ms", "ttft_ms", "output_tok_s"]})
        summaries.append(summary)
        (out / "summary.json").write_text(json.dumps(summaries, indent=2))
        print(length, batch, summary["median"], flush=True)

## Details

This extends the merged [#51012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51012) design to XPU. Unlike [#61163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61163), which installs a compiler pass, this dispatches the companion [kernel #670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/670) directly from the eager model. The companion PR is currently open; wheels without its provider use the existing MoE path.

Shared projections must use `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`; explicit W8A8 selection retains its activation quantization through the fallback. The performance and evaluation tables above retain their stated original measurement revisions.

AI assistance was used to implement, review and validate this change.

Hi @jikunshang , both AMD/Kimi K3 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode) and NVIDIA/DeepSeek V4.1

  initialization, weight qualification and runtime dispatch:

  • Initialization: hooks.py builds FusedMoeDecode exclusively through the existing model post-load hook, after quantization and before graph capture. Forward never initializes executors or prepares weights. This follows the separation illustrated by AMD’s hooks
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/hooks.py) and the post-load construction in NVIDIA’s model state
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/runtime/model_state.py#L62-L82). XPU uses standard model post-load hooks without a Model Runner V2-specific ModelState dependency.

  • Weight qualification/preparation: weights.py checks static configuration, backend, dtype and layout eligibility, informed by AMD’s weight guards
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/guards.py#L15-L94). Necessary contiguous model-owned layouts are prepared before executor binding. Static initialization failures report a fallback
    reason once.

  • Runtime dispatch: FusedMoeDecode checks the current input in vLLM, including 1–8 token rows and rows * top_k <= 512, before calling the fused provider. Ineligible or uninitialized calls use the existing MoE forward. This follows the guarded dispatch/fallback patterns in NVIDIA’s
    MoEStep (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/moe/step.py#L72-L103) and AMD’s decode planning
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/decode.py#L155-L192).

  • Parameter ownership: After preparation, the executor directly references model-owned tensors. Supported in-place kernel-format reloads remain visible to captured graphs. Changes to storage, layout or eligibility require rebuilding the executor and recapturing graphs.

  The XPU model and MTP implementations remain independent. Fusion covers local routed/shared expert computation; routing/top-k and the single final TP reduction remain in vLLM. This revision leaves native kernel math unchanged.

detail.body:
## Overview

Move Qwen3.5 models and MTP on XPU to the eager, breakable-graph design introduced by [vLLM #51012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51012). Recover small-batch MoE decode fusion by calling the routed/shared expert provider from [vllm-xpu-kernels #670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/670) directly in the XPU model, without model-level `torch.compile` or a compiler fusion pass. Fusion is bounded to eligible 1–8-token FP16/BF16 calls with per-tensor FP8-e4m3 weights; the routed/shared expert outputs share one TP reduction. Other configurations retain the existing MoE path.

## Claims

- TP2, async, graph-on MoE B1: streamed TPOT **-21.0% to -20.1%**, output throughput **+16.3% to +25.4%** for 1K/8K/32K input and 512 output tokens versus the compiled XPU baseline.

## Validation

Environment: two Intel Xe2 GPUs, 32 GB per card, cards 0/1, TP2, PyTorch `2.14.0+xpu`, FP16 with online `fp8_per_tensor` quantization. Performance checkpoints: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE)**, using the Qwen3.5 implementation, and **Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B**, measured at **BF16, no quantization, TP1 on card 0**, with TP2 greedy checks on cards 0/1.

Baseline: main `fa3b9d1377`, original XPU model with `VLLM_COMPILE` (mode 3). This PR: `dd6f1ccb15`, XPU eager model (mode 0). Both use the same kernel build (`0becdcc76c`, the #670 Qwen native implementations). Matching serving flags: async scheduling, prefix caching off, block size 64, max model length 40960, max batched tokens 8192 and max sequences 128. Offline runs use max sequences 32. Graph-on is `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

### End-to-end serving (`vllm bench serve`)

Random workload follows #51012: 320/384/512 prompts at concurrency 32/64/128, 128-token input and 256-token output; 128 prompts at cc32 for the 4K-context case; 16 prompts for single-stream decode and 4K/8 prefill. Real MoE prompts use a fixed, balanced 32-row subset of SPEED-Bench `throughput_8k`, 512 output tokens; this is a subset measurement.

| 9B BF16 TP1 | decode cc64 | ITL | 47.99 | 47.79 | -0.4% | +0.4% |
| 9B BF16 TP1 | decode cc128 | ITL | 60.58 | 63.71 | +5.2% | +12.8% |
| 9B BF16 TP1 | decode 4k, cc32 | ITL | 93.65 | 93.24 | -0.4% | +0.5% |
| 9B BF16 TP1 | decode cc1 | ITL | 28.38 | 28.45 | +0.3% | -0.3% |

## Details

This extends the merged [#51012](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51012) design to XPU. Unlike [#61163](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61163), which installs a compiler pass, this dispatches the companion [kernel #670](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-xpu-kernels/pull/670) directly from the eager model. The companion PR is currently open; wheels without its provider use the existing MoE path.

Shared projections must use `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`; explicit W8A8 selection retains its activation quantization through the fallback. The performance and evaluation tables above retain their stated original measurement revisions.

AI assistance was used to implement, review and validate this change.

+### Qwen3.5 eager execution and MoE decode fusion
+
+Qwen3.5 dense, MoE and MTP models on XPU use the dedicated eager implementation.
+Breakable graphs are enabled by default for these architectures, and model-level
+`torch.compile` is disabled. No environment variable is required to select this
+execution path. ROCm and other fallback platforms retain their existing model
+implementations.
+
+The routed/shared expert fusion is optional. It requires a companion
+`vllm-xpu-kernels` build providing
+`vllm_xpu_kernels.moe_shared_fused_interface.XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert` and the native
+`torch.ops._xpu_C.moe_shared_fused_decode_interface` operator. A build without
+this provider uses the existing MoE implementation. The model's
+`xpu/specialized_decode` modules qualify loaded weights and bind an executor
+after quantization, before graph capture. Runtime token-row eligibility is
+checked in vLLM before dispatching the fused operator.
+Failed static checks report a fallback reason once during initialization.
+Fusion is enabled by default when the provider and configuration qualify.
+
+Fusion applies to eligible calls with **1–8 input token rows**, contiguous,
+64-byte-aligned FP16/BF16 activations, `rows * top_k <= 512`,
+FP8-e4m3 routed/shared weights with FP32
+per-expert/per-tensor scales, matching expert dimensions and a supported routing
+configuration. Both shared projections must use `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`.
+Explicit `--linear-backend=xpu` selects W8A8 activation quantization and keeps
+these projections on the existing MoE path. Tensor parallelism uses one
+reduction for the combined routed and shared outputs. Larger token batches,
+other quantization formats and
+unsupported features such as LoRA, expert/sequence parallelism, DBO or EPLB use
+the existing MoE path. Dense models do not use this expert fusion.
+
+For example, with the companion provider installed:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B \
+  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8_per_tensor \
+  --compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
+```
+
+To run eager inference without graph capture, set
+`--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'`. This keeps the XPU
+model implementation and eligible MoE fusion. The executor reads model-owned
+parameters directly, so in-place weight reloads/updates are visible to captured
+graphs without a worker refresh callback. Changes to weight storage, metadata
+or fusion eligibility require rebuilding the executor and recapturing graphs.
+
+`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` is a graph mode and can use the breakable XPU-graph capture
+mechanism. The post-load hook prepares necessary contiguous parameter layouts
+before binding the executor; forward does not initialize or prepare weights.
+The fused and stock paths can differ in accumulation order and intermediate
+rounding. This model integration uses standard post-load hooks and has no
+Model Runner V2-only dependency.
+

+        self.vocab_size = config.vocab_size
+
+        self.mtp_start_layer_idx = config.num_hidden_layers
+        self.num_mtp_layers = getattr(config, "mtp_num_hidden_layers", 1)
+
+        self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(
+            self.vocab_size,
+            config.hidden_size,
+        )
+
+        # Workaround: mtp.fc is stored as BF16 in NVFP4 checkpoints but is
+        # missing from hf_quant_config.json exclude_modules. Force unquantized.
+        # Ref: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/38650
+        # Ref: https://github.com/NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer/pull/1124
+        fc_quant = (
+            None
+            if (quant_config and quant_config.get_name() == "modelopt_fp4")
+            else quant_config
+        )
+        self.fc = ColumnParallelLinear(
+            self.config.hidden_size * 2,
+            self.config.hidden_size,
+            gather_output=True,
+            bias=False,
+            return_bias=False,
+            quant_config=fc_quant,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.fc",
+        )
+
+        # GPTQ: quantized checkpoints may exclude MTP from quantization via
+        # quantization_config.dynamic with "-:pattern" entries. When detected,
+        # disable quantization for MTP layers so they use unquantized params.
+        original_quant = vllm_config.quant_config
+        if quant_config and quant_config.get_name() not in ("modelopt_fp4",):
+            hf_qc = getattr(model_config.hf_config, "quantization_config", None)
+            if isinstance(hf_qc, dict):
+                dynamic = hf_qc.get("dynamic", {})
+                if any(k.startswith("-:") and "mtp" in k for k in dynamic):
+                    vllm_config.quant_config = None
+        self.layers = torch.nn.ModuleList(
+            Qwen3_5DecoderLayer(
+                vllm_config,
+                layer_type="full_attention",
+                prefix=f"{prefix}.layers.{idx}",
+            )
+            for idx in range(self.num_mtp_layers)
+        )
+        vllm_config.quant_config = original_quant
+        self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors = make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(
+            ["hidden_states", "residual"], config.hidden_size
+        )
+        self.norm = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps)
+        self.pre_fc_norm_hidden = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(
+            config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+        self.pre_fc_norm_embedding = Qwen3_5RMSNorm(
+            config.hidden_size, eps=config.rms_norm_eps
+        )
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        spec_step_idx: int = 0,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # Branch on the inputs, not the rank: the drafter is built entirely on
+        # the last PP stage, where `is_first_rank` is False.
+        if intermediate_tensors is None:
+            if inputs_embeds is None:
+                inputs_embeds = self.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+            assert hidden_states.shape[-1] == inputs_embeds.shape[-1]
+            hidden_states = torch.cat(
+                [
+                    self.pre_fc_norm_embedding(inputs_embeds),
+                    self.pre_fc_norm_hidden(hidden_states),
+                ],
+                dim=-1,
+            )
+            hidden_states = self.fc(hidden_states)
+            residual = None
+        else:
+            hidden_states = intermediate_tensors["hidden_states"]
+            residual = intermediate_tensors["residual"]
+
+        current_step_idx = spec_step_idx % self.num_mtp_layers
+        mtp_layer = self.layers[current_step_idx]
+        if mtp_layer.use_attn_reduce_scatter_for_moe:
+            assert hidden_states.shape[0] == positions.shape[-1]
+            hidden_states = sequence_parallel_chunk(hidden_states)
+            assert residual is None
+        hidden_states, residual = mtp_layer(
+            positions=positions,
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            residual=residual,
+        )
+
+        if not get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            return IntermediateTensors(
+                {"hidden_states": hidden_states, "residual": residual}
+            )
+
+        hidden_states, _ = self.norm(hidden_states, residual)
+        if mtp_layer.use_attn_reduce_scatter_for_moe:
+            hidden_states = tensor_model_parallel_all_gather(hidden_states, 0)
+            hidden_states = hidden_states[: positions.shape[-1]]
+        return hidden_states
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        return loader.load_weights(weights, mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+
+
+class Qwen3_5MTP(LocalArgmaxMixin, nn.Module, SupportsMultiModal, SupportsPP):
+    def process_weights_after_loading(self) -> None:
+        initialize_specialized_decode(self)
+
+    packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": [
+            "q_proj",
+            "k_proj",
+            "v_proj",
+        ],
+        "gate_up_proj": ["gate_proj", "up_proj"],
+    }

+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_text_config

+        self.quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+
+        super().__init__()
+        self.config = config
+        self.model = Qwen3_5MultiTokenPredictor(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "mtp")
+        )
+
+        if get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            self.lm_head = ParallelLMHead(
+                config.vocab_size,
+                config.hidden_size,
+                quant_config=self.quant_config,
+                prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head"),
+            )
+            if config.tie_word_embeddings:
+                self.lm_head = self.lm_head.tie_weights(self.model.embed_tokens)
+        else:
+            self.lm_head = PPMissingLayer()
+
+        self.logits_processor = LogitsProcessor(config.vocab_size)
+
+        self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors = (
+            self.model.make_empty_intermediate_tensors
+        )
+
+    def embed_input_ids(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        multimodal_embeddings: MultiModalEmbeddings | None = None,
+        *,
+        is_multimodal: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        inputs_embeds = self._embed_text_input_ids(
+            input_ids,
+            self.model.embed_input_ids,
+            is_multimodal=is_multimodal,
+        )
+
+        if multimodal_embeddings is None or len(multimodal_embeddings) == 0:
+            return inputs_embeds
+
+        is_multimodal = _require_is_multimodal(is_multimodal)
+
+        inputs_embeds = _merge_multimodal_embeddings(
+            inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds,
+            multimodal_embeddings=multimodal_embeddings,
+            is_multimodal=is_multimodal,
+        )
+
+        return inputs_embeds
+
+    def forward(  # type: ignore[override]
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        **kwargs: object,
+    ):
+        hidden_states = self.model(
+            input_ids, positions, hidden_states, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds
+        )
+        return hidden_states
+
+    def compute_logits(
+        self,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        spec_step_idx: int = 0,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        return self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)
+
+    def is_unused_checkpoint_weight(self, name: str) -> bool:
+        return not name.startswith("mtp.") and not any(
+            key in name for key in ["embed_tokens", "lm_head"]
+        )
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        def remap_weight_names(weights):
+            for name, weight in weights:
+                if self.is_unused_checkpoint_weight(name):
+                    continue
+                if name.startswith("mtp."):
+                    name = name.replace("mtp.", "model.")
+                elif "embed_tokens" in name:
+                    name = name.replace("language_model.", "")
+                yield name, weight
+
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        return loader.load_weights(remap_weight_names(weights))
+
+

+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__(vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=prefix)
+        self.set_moe_parameters()

+# Qwen3.5 XPU fused MoE decode
+
+This package accelerates small-row routed and sigmoid-gated shared experts in
+the dedicated XPU eager model. Eligible calls use the native
+`XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert` provider from `vllm-xpu-kernels`; other calls use the
+existing `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` implementation. Dense models are unaffected.
+
+## Scope and fallback
+
+Eligibility is based on input token rows, including speculative verification
+rows, rather than request concurrency. Calls require 1–8 rows and
+`rows * top_k <= 512`. An eligible short prefill can also use the same operator.
+Inputs must be rank-two, contiguous, 64-byte-aligned FP16/BF16 tensors with the
+configured hidden dimension, dtype and weight device.
+
+Static eligibility is checked after weight loading:
+
+- The routed backend is `XPUExpertsFp8`; both shared projections use
+  `XPUW8A16FP8LinearKernel`. W8A8 shared projections retain their activation
+  quantization through the stock path.
+- Routed weights are FP8-e4m3 tensors shaped `[E, H, 2I]` and `[E, I, H]`, with
+  one FP32 scale per expert. Shared weights have matching `[H, 2I]` and `[I, H]`
+  shapes, each with one FP32 scale. The shared gate is `[H]` or `[1, H]`, with
+  the activation dtype. All tensors are on the same XPU device.
+- `1 <= top_k <= E <= 512`; `H` and `I` are positive multiples of 32. The native
+  block-2D descriptor limits require `2H <= 2^24 - 1` and `4I <= 2^24 - 1`.
+  The installed provider must support the weight device through its native
+  Xe2/Xe3 dispatcher.
+- Routed and shared experts use SiLU without bias, unit routed scaling and
+  router weights applied to expert outputs. The stock router still selects
+  the experts.
+- Sequence/expert/data/prefill-context parallelism, expert maps, EPLB, DBO,
+  LoRA, routed input/output transforms, zero-expert routing, replicated shared
+  experts and an already-enabled shared-expert fusion use the stock path.
+- Contiguous weight matrices require 64-byte alignment; the contiguous shared
+  gate requires 32-byte alignment. Eligible non-contiguous parameters are
+  made contiguous during post-load preparation.
+
+Missing providers and failed static checks emit a reason once during
+initialization. Runtime row, shape, device, dtype, contiguity and alignment
+checks silently select the stock path when a call is ineligible. Forward also
+uses stock when the post-load hook has not initialized an executor.
+
+## Default behavior and numerics
+
+Fusion is enabled by default when the provider and model configuration qualify.
+It replaces local expert computation and preserves the stock router and final
+reduction contract: the combined routed/shared output receives one standard TP
+all-reduce when that reduction is required. Under the supported configurations,
+either local path reaches the same collective, so no additional TP agreement or
+kernel peer-communication protocol is needed. This layer optimization has no
+whole-model decode selector or persistent communication kernel.
+No additional specialized-decode fail-stop mechanism is needed because the
+provider introduces no kernel peer-communication protocol. Native execution
+errors retain normal worker error handling.
+
+The fused and stock kernels can differ in accumulation order and intermediate
+rounding. Shared projections retain FP16/BF16 activations on both paths;
+activation quantization is not bypassed for a W8A8 backend. Bitwise equality or
+full-model accuracy parity is not assumed. Correctness tests compare native
+outputs against the stock block with numerical tolerances; model validation
+also checks greedy outputs and logprob compatibility.
+
+## Lifecycle and graphs
+
+The model loader finishes per-layer quantization before calling
+`process_weights_after_loading()`. The hook then qualifies static configuration
+and weights, prepares necessary contiguous model-owned parameters, and binds
+the executor. Graph capture and any other consumers binding parameter storage
+must run after this preparation. Forward never constructs an executor or
+replaces parameters.
+
+`replace_parameter()` preserves parameter objects and reload metadata where
+supported; initial layout preparation can change storage or strides. It must
+therefore precede address binding. Subsequent in-place kernel-format reloads
+are visible through the model-owned tensors, including captured graphs.
+Storage, layout or eligibility changes require rebuilding the executor and
+recapturing graphs.
+
+The eager model supports graph-off execution and breakable XPU graphs.
+`FULL_DECODE_ONLY` selects decode capture; breakable graphs describe the capture
+mechanism, and can be used with that mode. This package uses model post-load
+hooks and tensor metadata, with no Model Runner V2-only `ModelState` dependency.
+
+## Layout
+
+- `__init__.py`: package scope and token-row limits.
+- `hooks.py`: `initialize_specialized_decode()` post-load entry point for the
+  target and MTP models.
+- `weights.py`: static qualification and model-owned layout preparation.
+- `moe.py`: `FusedMoeDecode`, runtime eligibility, stock routing, native dispatch
+  and the final TP reduction.
+- `../model.py` and `../mtp.py`: eager model integration through post-load hooks
+  and the MoE block's forward call.
+
+Layer tests live in `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py`; model loading, graph reload
+and backend fallback tests live in
+`tests/models/qwen3_5/xpu_specialized_decode/test_integration.py`.

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Bind and execute routed + gated shared experts for eligible decode rows."""
+
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, cast
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed import tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.runner.moe_runner import MoERunner
+
+from . import MAX_DECODE_ROWS, MAX_ROUTED_ROWS
+from .weights import get_weights, prepare_weights
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm_xpu_kernels.moe_shared_fused_interface import XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert
+
+    from ..model import Qwen3_5SparseMoeBlock
+
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class FusedMoeDecode:
+    """A native MoE executor bound to one block's loaded parameters."""
+
+    def __init__(self, block: "Qwen3_5SparseMoeBlock"):
+        self.block = block
+        self.plan: XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert | None = None
+        self._weights: tuple[torch.Tensor, ...] | None = None
+        self.dtype: torch.dtype | None = None
+        self.hidden_dim = self.top_k = 0
+        weights = get_weights(block)
+        if isinstance(weights, str):
+            logger.info_once("Qwen3.5 XPU fused MoE disabled: %s", weights)
+            return
+        self._weights = weights
+        config = cast(MoERunner, block.experts).moe_config
+        self.dtype = config.in_dtype
+        self.hidden_dim = config.hidden_dim
+        self.top_k = config.experts_per_token
+        try:
+            from vllm_xpu_kernels.moe_shared_fused_interface import (
+                XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert as FusedMoe,
+            )
+            from vllm_xpu_kernels.moe_shared_fused_interface import (
+                supports,
+            )
+        except ImportError:
+            logger.info_once("Qwen3.5 XPU fused MoE disabled: provider unavailable")
+            self._weights = None
+            return
+        if not supports(
+            self.dtype,
+            self._weights[0].dtype,
+            self.top_k,
+            self.hidden_dim,
+            self._weights[1].shape[1],
+            device=self._weights[0].device,
+        ):
+            logger.info_once(
+                "Qwen3.5 XPU fused MoE disabled: native provider does not support "
+                "the weight device, dtype or dimensions"
+            )
+            return
+        weights = prepare_weights(self.block)
+        if isinstance(weights, str):
+            logger.info_once("Qwen3.5 XPU fused MoE disabled: %s", weights)
+            return
+        self._weights = weights
+        w13, w2, shared_w13, shared_w2, s13, s2, shared_s13, shared_s2, gate = (
+            self._weights
+        )
+        self.plan = FusedMoe(
+            w13=w13,
+            w13_scales=s13,
+            w2=w2,
+            w2_scales=s2,
+            shared_w13=shared_w13,
+            shared_w13_scale=shared_s13,
+            shared_w2=shared_w2,
+            shared_w2_scale=shared_s2,
+            shared_gate=gate,
+            top_k=self.top_k,
+        )
+
+    def get_plan(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> "XpuFusedMoeWithSharedExpert | None":
+        if (
+            self.plan is None
+            or x.device != self.plan.device
+            or x.ndim != 2
+            or not 1 <= x.shape[0] <= MAX_DECODE_ROWS
+            or x.shape[0] * self.top_k > MAX_ROUTED_ROWS
+            or x.shape[1] != self.hidden_dim
+            or x.dtype != self.dtype
+            or not x.is_contiguous()
+            or x.data_ptr() % 64
+        ):
+            return None
+        return self.plan
+
+    def run(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
+        plan = self.get_plan(hidden_states)
+        if plan is None:
+            return None
+        block = self.block
+        runner = cast(MoERunner, block.experts)
+        router_logits, _ = block.gate(hidden_states)
+        topk_weights, topk_ids = runner.router.select_experts(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            router_logits=router_logits,
+            topk_indices_dtype=runner.routed_experts.quant_method.topk_indices_dtype,
+            input_ids=None,
+        )
+        output = plan.forward(
+            torch.empty_like(hidden_states),
+            hidden_states,
+            topk_weights.to(torch.float32).contiguous(),
+            topk_ids.contiguous(),
+        )
+        if block.tp_size > 1 and not runner.moe_config.skip_final_all_reduce:
+            output = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(output)
+        return output

Hi @jikunshang , both AMD/Kimi K3 (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode) and NVIDIA/DeepSeek V4.1

  initialization, weight qualification and runtime dispatch:

  • Initialization: hooks.py builds FusedMoeDecode exclusively through the existing model post-load hook, after quantization and before graph capture. Forward never initializes executors or prepares weights. This follows the separation illustrated by AMD’s hooks
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/hooks.py) and the post-load construction in NVIDIA’s model state
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/runtime/model_state.py#L62-L82). XPU uses standard model post-load hooks without a Model Runner V2-specific ModelState dependency.

  • Weight qualification/preparation: weights.py checks static configuration, backend, dtype and layout eligibility, informed by AMD’s weight guards
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/guards.py#L15-L94). Necessary contiguous model-owned layouts are prepared before executor binding. Static initialization failures report a fallback
    reason once.

  • Runtime dispatch: FusedMoeDecode checks the current input in vLLM, including 1–8 token rows and rows * top_k <= 512, before calling the fused provider. Ineligible or uninitialized calls use the existing MoE forward. This follows the guarded dispatch/fallback patterns in NVIDIA’s
    MoEStep (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/moe/step.py#L72-L103) and AMD’s decode planning
    (https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/de53c2deed03abd19cdef4f2bddcfcef60a84610/vllm/models/kimi_k3/amd/specialized_decode/runtime/decode.py#L155-L192).

  • Parameter ownership: After preparation, the executor directly references model-owned tensors. Supported in-place kernel-format reloads remain visible to captured graphs. Changes to storage, layout or eligibility require rebuilding the executor and recapturing graphs.

  The XPU model and MTP implementations remain independent. Fusion covers local routed/shared expert computation; routing/top-k and the single final TP reduction remain in vLLM. This revision leaves native kernel math unchanged.
